base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and set up a home security system. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I just moved into a new house and I'm looking at home security systems. Narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 home security systems: SecureHome Pro, GuardShield Plus, SafeNest Basic

SecureHome Pro: professional installation, 24/7 monitoring, $280/year subscription. GuardShield Plus: weekend technician install, advanced sensors and cameras, $180/year subscription. SafeNest Basic: DIY self-install, app-based monitoring with smart alerts, $65/year subscription.
SecureHome Pro equipment kit: $450 upfront. GuardShield Plus equipment kit: $320 upfront. SafeNest Basic equipment kit: $150 upfront.
User works from home on weekdays, free on weekends

constraints.value: Maximum first-year total spend is $240. Derived from monthly take-home of $3600, household rule is no more than one month's grocery budget on security, and groceries run $120/month, so 2 months of groceries = $240 cap for the entire first year (equipment + subscription combined).
constraints.surface_form: My monthly take-home is $3600. My wife and I have a rule — we won't spend more than two months of groceries on home security for the first year, equipment and subscription combined. Our groceries run about $120 a month.

constraints.value: Cannot be home on weekdays for a technician visit because user works from home and has back-to-back video calls all day — cannot have installation noise or interruptions. Weekends are free.
constraints.surface_form: I work from home but honestly my weekdays are wall-to-wall video calls, I can't have someone drilling and installing stuff while I'm on camera. Weekends are totally free though.
inference_chain: Works from home with back-to-back video calls on weekdays → cannot accommodate noisy installation during weekdays
SecureHome Pro uses professional installation scheduled on weekdays → eliminated by schedule
GuardShield Plus uses weekend technician install → schedule OK
SafeNest Basic is DIY self-install → can do on weekend, schedule OK

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 home security systems (SecureHome Pro, GuardShield Plus, SafeNest Basic). You will share system details, prices, your budget, and your schedule constraints across several turns. Your neighbor and your brother will praise SecureHome Pro and GuardShield Plus respectively. At the very end, you will simply say you have made your decision and need to finalize your order this week — you must NEVER name which system you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, matter-of-fact homeowner. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience, even if the assistant asks clarifying questions. You treat each part of the conversation as normal planning.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak the answer or cause identity confusion

aims.description: I just moved into a new house and I'm looking at home security systems. I've narrowed it down to three: SecureHome Pro, GuardShield Plus, and SafeNest Basic.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option security system selection

aims.description: So here's what I've got: SecureHome Pro does professional installation, 24/7 monitoring, $280 a year subscription, and the equipment kit is $450 upfront. GuardShield Plus has a weekend technician install, advanced sensors and cameras, $180 a year, equipment is $320 upfront. SafeNest Basic is DIY self-install, app-based monitoring with smart alerts, $65 a year, and the equipment kit is $150 upfront.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 options with their subscription costs and equipment costs
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with subscription prices and equipment costs in ONE turn

aims.description: My neighbor got SecureHome Pro installed last month. He showed me the app — the live camera feeds are crystal clear, and the response time from the monitoring center is under 30 seconds. He's really happy with it.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive SecureHome Pro review from the neighbor

drift_config.drift_topic: got SecureHome Pro installed, crystal clear camera feeds, monitoring center responds in under 30 seconds, very happy with it

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward SecureHome Pro

aims.description: My monthly take-home is $3600. My wife and I have a rule — we won't spend more than two months of groceries on home security for the first year, equipment and subscription combined. Our groceries run about $120 a month.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the budget information and ideally computes the $240 cap, eliminating SecureHome Pro ($450+$280=$730) and GuardShield Plus ($320+$180=$500)
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via computation — agent must derive $120 × 2 = $240 cap

aims.description: My neighbor was also telling me SecureHome Pro caught a package thief on his porch last week. The monitoring center called the police before he even noticed. Pretty impressive honestly.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the SecureHome Pro package theft story

drift_config.drift_topic: SecureHome Pro caught a package thief, monitoring center called police automatically

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about SecureHome Pro (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I work from home but honestly my weekdays are wall-to-wall video calls, I can't have someone drilling and installing stuff while I'm on camera. Weekends are totally free though.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this eliminates SecureHome Pro (professional weekday installation) as an option
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver schedule constraint — double-eliminates SecureHome Pro (weekday install + over budget)

aims.description: My brother just upgraded to GuardShield Plus at his place. He said the motion sensors are way more accurate than his old system, almost zero false alarms. His wife used to complain about the alerts going off for raccoons, but not anymore.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive GuardShield Plus review from the brother

drift_config.drift_topic: upgraded to GuardShield Plus, motion sensors very accurate, almost zero false alarms, wife no longer complains

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward GuardShield Plus

aims.description: My brother also mentioned GuardShield Plus integrates with his smart thermostat and door locks. He controls everything from one app now. Said it made his whole house feel way more connected.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to GuardShield Plus smart home integration features

drift_config.drift_topic: GuardShield Plus integrates with smart thermostat and door locks, single app controls everything, house feels more connected

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about GuardShield Plus (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: Alright I've made up my mind. I need to finalize my order this week. Which one should I go with?
aims.success_criteria: Agent commits to SafeNest Basic as the recommendation, showing that it is the only system where the first-year total ($150 equipment + $65 subscription = $215) falls within the $240 budget derived from $120 groceries × 2 months, and that it avoids the weekday installation conflict
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to the constraint-compliant option

ground_truth.answer: The user should go with SafeNest Basic ($150 equipment + $65/year subscription = $215 first-year total). SecureHome Pro ($450 + $280 = $730) and GuardShield Plus ($320 + $180 = $500) both far exceed the $240 budget. SecureHome Pro is also eliminated by the weekday installation conflict. Only SafeNest Basic ($215 < $240, DIY weekend install) survives both constraints.
required_elements: Agent commits to recommending SafeNest Basic as the system to order
Agent shows that the first-year budget cap is $240 by computing $120 groceries per month × 2 months = $240
Agent shows that SecureHome Pro's first-year total ($450 equipment + $280 subscription = $730) exceeds the derived $240 budget cap
Agent shows that GuardShield Plus's first-year total ($320 equipment + $180 subscription = $500) exceeds the derived $240 budget cap
Agent shows that SafeNest Basic's first-year total ($150 equipment + $65 subscription = $215) falls within the $240 budget cap
forbidden_elements: Recommending SecureHome Pro ($730 first-year total far exceeds $240 budget, also requires weekday professional installation conflicting with video call schedule)
Recommending GuardShield Plus ($500 first-year total far exceeds $240 budget)
Ignoring the budget constraint and recommending based on features or recency of discussion alone
Asking the user which system they decided on instead of computing the answer from constraints
Presenting all three options as viable without eliminating the over-budget ones
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: groceries $120/month × 2 months = $240 first-year cap. SecureHome Pro: $450+$280=$730 (3× over budget). GuardShield Plus: $320+$180=$500 (2× over budget). SafeNest Basic: $150+$65=$215 (within budget). Schedule constraint: weekday video calls block weekday installation → SecureHome Pro double-eliminated. GuardShield Plus has weekend technician install (schedule OK) but still over budget. SafeNest Basic is DIY (weekend OK) and within budget. Despite 4 drift turns praising SecureHome Pro and GuardShield Plus, the agent must respect the hard constraints and recommend SafeNest Basic.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
